author: Linnaeus, 1758
summary: 국내에서는 함경남도와 강원도에서 발견된 기록이 있다. 높은 산의 바위 벽 가운데 선반처럼 튀어나온 자리에 둥지를 틀고, 한배에 알 1~2개를 낳지만 대개 1개만 깨어난다. 주로 동물의 사체를 먹는데, 먹이를 높은 데서 떨어뜨려 부서진 뼈에서 골수를 빼 먹으며 거북도 이렇게 깨뜨려 먹는다. 국외에서는 알타이, 중국, 몽골, 에스파냐, 모로코, 북아프리카, 티베트에 분포한다.

points.en: black stripe through the eye forming a 'beard'

art.subject: Bearded Vulture (Gypaetus barbatus), adult: head and neck creamy white, often stained orange-rust; a black mask runs from the bill base through the eye and ends in a tuft of black bristles hanging below the bill like a beard; breast and underparts rich tawny-orange to rusty-buff; upperparts, wings and tail dark slate-grey looking blackish, with fine white shaft streaks on the mantle and wing coverts. Bill greyish horn; iris pale yellow encircled by a bright red ring; legs feathered rusty-buff down to the toes, feet grey.
art.pose: gliding along a cliff face on long narrow wings
art.scene: Korean high mountains: sheer rock walls with narrow ledges; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched on a rock ledge: creamy-white head stained rusty, black mask through the eye ending in a black bristle beard, red ring around the pale eye, tawny-orange breast and belly, blackish-grey upperparts with fine white streaks, long tail
adult, flight seen from below: long, narrow, pointed dark wings, long wedge-shaped dark tail, tawny-orange body contrasting with the dark underwing, pale head with black beard
art.build: Huge, long-winged and long-tailed vulture, about 110cm, larger than a Golden Eagle and close to a Cinereous Vulture in length but much slimmer; the head is fully feathered, not bald. Bill large, strong and hooked, about as long as the head, with the black bristle beard below it. Legs short and shaggily feathered. In flight long, narrow, pointed wings and a long wedge-shaped tail give a giant falcon-like silhouette; glides along cliffs with few wingbeats.
avoid: Do not paint a bald or downy head; the head is fully feathered and pale.
Do not paint a grey head; the adult head is creamy white, often rust-stained.
Do not paint a broad-winged, short-tailed griffon silhouette; the wings are narrow and the tail long and wedge-shaped.
Do not paint a dark brown head and body; that is the juvenile, not the adult.
